Andrea — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. I pulled the files and am looping in Kimberly (privacy engineering) and Markus (legal) to confirm the transfer posture and subprocessors. Quick answers up front so you can plan the procurement: 

- Redwood’s baseline is to execute the EU SCCs (post-2020 template) and the UK IDTA (UK Addendum) when UK processing is in scope. Those are our standard inbound contractual safeguards.
- TIAs/DTIAs are typically requested by customers when: (a) the processing includes unencrypted direct identifiers leaving the EEA to jurisdictions without adequacy, or (b) a customer requires contractual evidence of additional technical measures beyond SCCs (e.g., dedicated on-prem key custody). From your description (pseudonymized metadata + on-EU storage) this may be \"SCCs + UK Addendum\" territory — but we need to validate the enrichment step to the UK.

Action items for us: I will attach our current subprocessors CSV and a short flow diagram showing region routing. Kimberly — can you confirm whether the enrichment routing to the UK triggers TIA-level safeguards for NovaMed? Markus — can you advise whether the EU SCCs + UK IDTA will be acceptable to NovaMed legal for the pilot or if they will insist on a TIA statement?

Attachment: flow_diagram_v1.png

Happy to set up 30 min tomorrow to walk through.

Thanks,
Olga
Olga Petrov

Andrea — quick technical confirmation from the privacy engineering side.

1) Routing and processing: for the configuration NovaMed described we can enforce region-restricted routing (EU-only storage + explicit routing rule to the UK for the enrichment partner). Routing is policy-based at the request layer and logged per-request for auditing. We can add a transient routing tag so you can prove the enrichment-only hop in logs.

2) Subprocessors: attaching our current subprocessor inventory (redwood_subprocessors.csv). Note that our cloud infra (AWS in eu-west-1) and the managed embeddings cache service are in scope. We can also provide the SOC 2 Type II report (redacted) under NDA.

3) TIA vs SCCs: based on the workflow (hashed keys, no direct identifiers) SCCs + UK IDTA should be sufficient for the pilot. If NovaMed legal prefers a TIA-style attestation, we can produce a concise attestation (1 page) that confirms: legal basis, restricted routing policy, retention windows, and that no downstream exports will be performed without explicit change control. That attestation is faster than a full DTIA and is how we handle several pilot customers.

Next steps (proposed):
- Redwood: provide final subprocessor CSV, SOC2 summary, and 1-page TIA attestation (if requested).
- NovaMed: confirm acceptance of SCCs + UK IDTA for pilot or request attestation.
- Schedule a 30-min call to sign off technical routing and retention.

Attachments: redwood_subprocessors.csv

Thanks,

Andrea / team — following up with a short legal proposal to avoid lengthy DTIA cycles for a short pilot. Proposed contractual paragraph to add to the DPA (we can insert as an addendum or DocuSign clause):

"For the purposes of the pilot under Deal NOVA-9872, the parties agree that processing of pseudonymized patient metadata shall be governed by the EU SCCs and the UK IDTA (where UK routing occurs). Redwood shall provide, prior to production onboarding, a current subprocessors list, SOC 2 Type II summary (redacted where necessary), and a one-page transfer attestation confirming: (i) routing is limited to the enrichment partner in the UK for the sole purpose of metadata augmentation; (ii) no direct identifiers will be exported from the EEA; and (iii) retention windows for augmented data will not exceed 90 days unless otherwise agreed in writing. The parties may revisit the need for a full TIA if the scope of processing materially changes."

If NovaMed legal agrees to that paragraph we can add it as an exhibit and proceed with SCC signature + UK Addendum execution. Andrea — if that works, can you confirm and we'll circulate a short DocuSign.

Markus
